entries.help:
Register a slash command (/ command) on the current bound Open Platform app; --force converts a name collision into an update (idempotent re-run)

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Use this for a new command name. On a name collision, update the existing command only when that is the user's intent.

Avoid when:
  • The command already exists and the user wants to edit it → use `+slash-command-update`.

Tips:
  • Changes may take about five minutes to appear in clients because of client-side caching; the server updates immediately.

Examples:
  • Create a localized slash command
      lark-cli application +slash-command-create --command greet --description "say hi" --description-i18n zh_cn=问候

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                      identity type: bot | user
      --command string                 command name WITHOUT the leading slash (server enforces uniqueness per app; max 100 commands)
      --description string             default description shown in the client command panel (description.default_value)
      --description-i18n stringArray   localized description, repeatable, format <lang>=<text> (e.g. zh_cn=发送问候); language codes are passed through to the server
      --dry-run                        print request without executing
      --force                          on name collision, resolve the existing command by name and update it in place
      --format string                  output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                           help for +slash-command-create
      --icon-key string                icon key (server default: skill_outlined; invalid keys are rejected server-side with code 40000031)
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json

entries.help:
Delete a slash command from the current bound app (high-risk: irreversible; recreating the same name yields a new command_id)

Risk: high-risk-write (requires explicit user confirmation to execute; the agent must NOT add --yes on its own — only pass --yes after the user has confirmed)

When to use:
  • Use this only after the user explicitly confirms the target and the irreversible deletion.

Prerequisites:
  • Explicit user confirmation is required before passing `--yes`; an agent must not self-approve the deletion.
  • Pass `--command-id` from `+slash-command-list`, or pass `--command` to let the CLI resolve the current id by name with a live list request.

Tips:
  • Deleted commands may linger in clients for about five minutes because of client-side caching.
  • Recreating the same command name produces a new `command_id`.

Examples:
  • Delete by name after explicit user confirmation
      lark-cli application +slash-command-delete --command greet --yes

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-delete [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: bot | user
      --command string      target command name WITHOUT leading slash (resolved via live list, needs read scope); mutually exclusive with --command-id
      --command-id string   target command_id; mutually exclusive with --command
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +slash-command-delete
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                shorthand for --format json
      --yes                 confirm high-risk operation

entries.help:
Update description / localized descriptions / icon of a slash command on the current bound app, addressed by --command-id or by name via --command

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Use this to change description, localized descriptions, or icon while retaining the command name and `command_id`.

Prerequisites:
  • Pass `--command-id` from `+slash-command-list`, or pass `--command` to let the CLI resolve the current id by name with a live list request.

Tips:
  • PATCH is field-level partial: fields you do not pass are preserved server-side.
  • The command name cannot be changed. Renaming means deleting and recreating the command, which produces a new `command_id`.

Examples:
  • Update by name (the CLI resolves the current command id first)
      lark-cli application +slash-command-update --command greet --description "new text"

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-update [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                      identity type: bot | user
      --command string                 target command name WITHOUT leading slash; resolved via live list (needs read scope); mutually exclusive with --command-id
      --command-id string              target command_id (from +slash-command-list or create output); mutually exclusive with --command
      --description string             new default description (description.default_value)
      --description-i18n stringArray   localized description, repeatable <lang>=<text>; REPLACES the whole i18n map (missing languages are dropped); requires --description
      --dry-run                        print request without executing
      --format string                  output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                           help for +slash-command-update
      --icon-key string                new icon key (invalid keys rejected server-side with code 40000031)
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json

entries.help:
Create an automation trigger (cron/record-change/webhook/feishu-approval); created disabled

Usage:
  lark-cli apps +automation-create [flags]

Flags:
      --app-id string                 Miaoda app id
      --approval-code string          [feishu-approval] approval definition code; omit to match all approval definitions
      --as string                     identity type: user
      --cron string                   [cron] 5-field cron expression, e.g. '0 9 * * *' (min interval 30m)
      --description string            optional description (<=50 chars)
      --dry-run                       print request without executing
      --event string                  [record-change] INSERT | UPDATE | UPSERT | DELETE
      --event-type string             [feishu-approval] approval_instance | approval_task
      --fields string                 [record-change] JSON array of field ids for UPDATE/UPSERT, ["*"] = all
      --format string                 output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                          help for +automation-create
      --instance-status stringArray   [feishu-approval] statuses for approval_instance
  -q, --jq string                     jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                          shorthand for --format json
      --name string                   trigger name (unique within app, <=100 chars)
      --status string                 optional initial status: enabled | disabled (default disabled; backend supports create+enable in one call)
      --table +db-table-list          [record-change] table name (from +db-table-list); dataloom tables key by name, not id
      --task-status stringArray       [feishu-approval] statuses for approval_task
      --timezone string               [cron] IANA timezone (default Asia/Shanghai)
      --trigger-type string           cron | record-change | webhook | feishu-approval
      --white-ip-list string          [webhook] JSON array of allowed IPs

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Example: lark-cli apps +automation-create --app-id <id> --name daily --trigger-type cron --cron '0 9 * * *'
    • Example: lark-cli apps +automation-create --app-id <id> --name onUpd --trigger-type record-change --table <tbl> --event UPDATE
    • Example: lark-cli apps +automation-create --app-id <id> --name hook --trigger-type webhook
    • Example: lark-cli apps +automation-create --app-id <id> --name apv --trigger-type feishu-approval --event-type approval_instance --instance-status APPROVED

      --as string              identity type: user

Risk: write

Tips:
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Order Count" --type statistics --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","data_sources":[{"table_name":"Orders","count_all":true}]}'
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Monthly sales" --type column --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","data_sources":[{"table_name":"Orders","series":[{"field_name":"Amount","rollup":"SUM"}],"group_by":[{"field_name":"Month","sort":{"type":"group","order":"asc"}}]}]}'
    • Chart blocks use multi-datasource data_config: one top-level base_token shared by all sources, with table_name/series/count_all/group_by/filter inside each data_sources[] element (text needs none). App block commands carry no --base-token.
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Notes" --type text --data-config '{"text":"# Sales overview"}'
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Open orders" --type list --sub-type standard --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","table_name":"Orders"}'
    • For list creates, omit optional columns/fields to use the product defaults. The CLI sends them only when explicitly provided.
    • Before creating data-backed blocks, use +table-list and +field-list to confirm real table and field names.
    • A list accepts exactly one base_token, and that Base must be in the same Workspace as the App.
    • Read lark-base-app-block-data-config.md as the SSOT for chart, list and text config; do not invent data_config from natural language.
    • Block type cannot be changed after creation and this phase has no delete command, so a wrong --type can only be fixed in the UI. Confirm the type before creating.
    • Widget layout, position, size and display settings are not part of the public create/update protocol; the platform applies product defaults.
    • Record block_id for +app-block-update. For chart data reads, pass the returned chart_token to +app-block-get-data --block-id.
    • Block names must be unique within the page; the CLI checks every existing block before creation.
    • Create blocks sequentially; do not parallelize multiple block creates for the same page.

    • +field-create defines storage schema only: choose a documented field type from explicit stored-value requirements and the user's semantics. Treat the field name or business purpose only as a clue to confirm; do not use it to invent derived behavior. Use style only to format the chosen type.
    • For explicitly requested derived, automatic, synchronized, or backfilled behavior, use documented formula, lookup, link, workflow, or automation only. If unsupported, do not probe code/web/OpenAPI, create a storage placeholder, or claim completion; report the boundary and alternatives.
    • Agent hint: for multiple fields in one table, prefer one array; array items are created sequentially.
    • For generated arrays, prefer --json @file or an argv-safe subprocess call; do not double-escape JSON inside shell command substitution.
    • For large arrays, bound successful stdout with --jq 'if .ok then (.data | {created,total,field_get_recommended,next_step,verification_hint}) else . end'; this preserves the full partial-failure envelope. Omit the projection when individual field IDs are needed.

Tips:
    • Happy path field: create_records is an array of independent record field maps.
    • Example: {"create_records":[{"Name":"Task A","Status":["Todo"]},{"Name":"Task B","Score":20}]}.

    • After batch-creating known helper rows, use the returned record IDs and your submitted rows; do not immediately +record-list the same table unless you need server-normalized formula/lookup values or failure diagnosis.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> ["Todo"] or ["Tag A","Tag B"] (when multiple=false, the array can contain only one option); datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.

entries.help:
Batch update records with record-specific fields

Usage:
  lark-cli base +record-batch-update [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot
      --base-token string   base token
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +record-batch-update
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json string         batch update JSON object; update_records maps each record ID to its field map, e.g. {"update_records":{"recA":{"Status":["Done"]},"recB":{"Score":20}}}
      --table-id string     table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Happy path field: update_records maps each record ID to its own field map.
    • Example: {"update_records":{"recA":{"Status":["Done"]},"recB":{"Score":20}}}.
    • The response contains only optional ignored_fields and does not check whether record IDs exist; read records back when confirmation is required.
    • Before writing, use +field-list to confirm real writable fields; do not write system fields, formula, lookup, or attachment fields as normal CellValue.
    • Batch update supports max 200 records per call.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> ["Todo"] or ["Tag A","Tag B"] (when multiple=false, the array can contain only one option); datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.
    • User and group fields always use arrays; when multiple=false, the array can contain only one item.
    • Do not guess user/chat/linked-record IDs or location coordinates; resolve them first with the relevant contact/im/record lookup flow.

Usage:
  lark-cli calendar +freebusy [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot

      --end string            end time (ISO 8601, default: end of start day)

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:

Risk: read

  • Before authoring `--content`, read the matching XML or Markdown guide under Related skills when available, unless already read. For XML, use only documented DocxXML tags.

entries.help:
One-way file-level mirror of a Drive folder onto a local directory (Drive → local)

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +pull [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --delete-local                 delete local regular files absent from Drive (file-level mirror; empty directories are NOT pruned); requires --yes
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          source Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +pull
      --if-exists string             policy when a local file already exists (skip = never touch existing files; smart = skip when local mtime is already up to date; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "overwrite")
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|rename|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --yes                          confirm --delete-local before deleting local files

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Only entries with type=file are downloaded; online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides) and shortcuts are skipped.
    • Subfolders recurse and are reproduced as local directories under --local-dir; missing parents are created automatically.
    • For repeat syncs, --if-exists=smart is the recommended best-effort incremental mode: it compares local mtime with Drive modified_time and skips downloads when the local copy is already up to date.
    • Duplicate remote rel_path conflicts fail by default. Use --on-duplicate-remote=rename to download duplicate files with stable hashed suffixes.
    • --delete-local requires --yes; without --yes the command is rejected upfront so a stray flag never deletes anything.

if-exists.description: policy when a Drive file already exists at the same rel_path (skip = never touch existing remote files; smart = skip when remote modified_time already matches or is newer, otherwise fall through to overwrite semantics; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "skip")

jq.description: jq expression to filter JSON output

on-duplicate-remote.description: policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")

entries.help:
File-level mirror of a local directory onto a Drive folder (local → Drive; remote-only directories are not removed)

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +push [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --delete-remote                delete Drive files absent locally (file-level mirror; remote-only directories are not removed); requires --yes
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          target Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +push
      --if-exists string             policy when a Drive file already exists at the same rel_path (skip = never touch existing remote files; smart = skip when remote modified_time already matches or is newer, otherwise fall through to overwrite semantics; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "skip")
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --yes                          confirm --delete-remote before deleting Drive files

Risk: write

Tips:
    • This is a file-level mirror: only type=file entries are uploaded, overwritten or deleted. Online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides), shortcuts, and remote-only directories are never touched.
    • Local directory structure (including empty directories) is mirrored to Drive via create_folder; existing remote folders are reused.
    • For repeat syncs, --if-exists=smart is a best-effort incremental mode: it compares local mtime with Drive modified_time and skips uploads when the remote copy is already up to date; otherwise it falls through to the same overwrite path as --if-exists=overwrite.
    • Duplicate remote rel_path conflicts fail by default before upload, overwrite, or delete. Use --on-duplicate-remote=newest|oldest only when the conflict is duplicate files and you explicitly want to target one.
    • Default --if-exists=skip is the safe choice while the upload_all overwrite-version field is rolling out. Pass --if-exists=overwrite to replace remote bytes; on tenants without the field it surfaces a structured api_error and the run exits non-zero. The same caveat applies when --if-exists=smart decides the remote file is older and falls through to overwrite.
    • --delete-remote requires --yes; without --yes the command is rejected upfront so a stray flag never deletes anything.
    • --delete-remote --yes also requires the space:document:delete scope. Validate runs a dynamic pre-flight check when the flag is on, so a missing grant fails the run before any upload — preventing a half-synced state where files were uploaded but the cleanup pass cannot delete.
    • Item-level failures (upload, overwrite, folder, delete) bump summary.failed and the run exits non-zero. If any upload or folder step fails, the --delete-remote phase is skipped entirely so a partial upload never triggers remote deletion.

Two-way sync between a local directory and a Drive folder

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +sync [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +sync
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-conflict string           conflict resolution when both sides modified a file (local-wins|remote-wins|keep-both|ask) (default "remote-wins")
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --quick                        use best-effort modified_time comparison instead of SHA-256 hash; mismatched timestamps can still trigger real sync writes

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Two-way sync: new remote files are pulled, new local files are pushed, and conflicts (both sides modified) are resolved by --on-conflict.
    • Default --on-conflict=remote-wins pulls the remote version when both sides changed a file. Use local-wins to push instead, keep-both to rename and keep both copies, or ask for interactive resolution.
    • Pass --quick for faster best-effort diff detection using modified_time instead of SHA-256 hash (no remote file downloads needed during diffing).
    • Because +sync acts on the diff, --quick can still pull, overwrite, or rename files when timestamps differ even if file contents are actually unchanged.
    • Actual sync execution pre-flights download, upload, and folder-create scopes before listing or walking, so missing grants fail before any partial sync can start.
    • Only entries with type=file are synced; online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides) and shortcuts are skipped.

  lark-cli drive +update-title [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                      identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                        print request without executing
      --format string                  output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                           help for +update-title
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json
      --on-extension-mismatch string   --type file only: keep appends the current extension when the title has none and rejects a different extension; allow submits the title verbatim without reading the current title (keep|allow) (default "keep")
      --title string                   new title to set; must not be empty
      --token string                   target token or URL; bare tokens require --type
      --type string                    target type for bare --token; optional for URLs but must match the URL type when provided (docx|sheet|bitable|base|slides|file|folder|wiki|apps|doc|mindnote)
      --url string                     recommended: Lark/Feishu URL of the target (docx/sheets/base/slides/file/folder/wiki)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • --type must match the real resource type; a mismatched type fails with 981003 not found, the same code an unknown token returns.
    • For a wiki node pass the node token from the /wiki/ URL with --type wiki; the underlying document token is not accepted there. Renaming either side keeps node and document titles in sync.
    • For --type file the title replaces the whole file name, extension included. By default the CLI reads the current name and appends its extension when the title has none, reporting it in the extension_appended output field; a title that changes the extension is rejected unless --on-extension-mismatch=allow.
    • An empty title is rejected locally; the API would accept it and leave the resource with a blank title.
    • Renames are rate limited (99991400): serialize bulk renames instead of running them in parallel, and retry later with exponential backoff.
    • 981004 forbidden means the identity lacks edit permission on the target, not a missing scope; the scope codes are 99991672 (app scope not applied) and 99991679 (user did not grant it).

entries.help:
Edit a sent text or rich-text message, optionally updating its attachment zone; bot only (the edit API does not accept user tokens)

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Use this to edit an already-sent **text or rich-text (post)** message, including its attachment zone.

Avoid when:
  • Editing an interactive card → use `messages patch`.
  • Sending a corrected message as a new message → use `+messages-send`.

Prerequisites:
  • Confirm the target message id, the new content, and that the calling identity (bot) is the original sender before editing.

Tips:
  • Omit attachment flags to preserve the current attachment zone.
  • `--set-attachments` replaces the attachment set; `--clear-attachments` removes it.
  • `--content` that already carries a `files` array cannot be combined with the attachment flags.

Examples:
  • Edit a message to a post with an attachment zone
      lark-cli im +messages-edit --as bot --message-id om_xxx --markdown "Updated content" --set-attachments file_xxx

enumDescriptions: Identifies a user to a tenant. The same user has different User IDs in different tenants. In one single tenant, a user has the same User ID in all apps （including store apps）. User ID is usually used to communicate user data between different apps.

Identifies a user to a tenant that acts as a developer. A user has the same Union ID in apps developed by the same developer, and has different Union IDs in apps developed by different developers. A developer can use Union ID to link the same user's identities in multiple apps.
Identifies a user to an app. The same user has different Open IDs in different apps.
The unique identifier of the Feishu open platform application. When an application is created, it is automatically generated by the system and cannot be modified by the user.

manager_ids.description: To set the administrator's ID, the ID type is consistent with the query parameter member_id_type value.; - If it is a user (member_id_type value is user_id/open_id/union_id), it is recommended to use the user's open_id.; Note:; - For ordinary groups, up to 10 administrators can be specified.;- For super large groups, up to 20 administrators can be specified.;- When making a single request to specify robots, up to 5 bots can be specified

enumDescriptions: Identifies a user to a tenant. The same user has different User IDs in different tenants. In one single tenant, a user has the same User ID in all apps （including store apps）. User ID is usually used to communicate user data between different apps.

Identifies a user to a tenant that acts as a developer. A user has the same Union ID in apps developed by the same developer, and has different Union IDs in apps developed by different developers. A developer can use Union ID to link the same user's identities in multiple apps.
Identifies a user to an app. The same user has different Open IDs in different apps.

Identifies a user to a tenant that acts as a developer. A user has the same Union ID in apps developed by the same developer, and has different Union IDs in apps developed by different developers. A developer can use Union ID to link the same user's identities in multiple apps.

Identifies group chats by chat_id. You can call the API Search for groups visible to a user or bot to obtain the chat_id value.

Identifies thread by thread_id.

entries.description: Use when updating an existing mail draft without sending it. Prefer this shortcut over calling raw drafts.get or drafts.update directly, because it performs draft-safe MIME read/patch/write editing while preserving unchanged structure, attachments, and headers where possible.

body.description: Full email body for a complete replacement (set_body). Prefer HTML for rich formatting (bold, lists, links); plain text is also supported. Body type is auto-detected. Use --patch-file with set_reply_body when you need to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block; use --body when you want a full body replacement. Mutually exclusive with --body-file. Cannot be combined with --patch-file body ops.

body-file.description: Path (relative, within cwd subtree) to a file containing the email body HTML. Mutually exclusive with --body. Size capped at 32 MB. (supports @file)

draft-id.description: Target draft ID. Required for real edits. It can be omitted only when using the --print-patch-template flag by itself.

format.description: output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")

from.description: Mailbox email address containing the draft (default: me). Prefer --mailbox for clarity; --from is kept for backward compatibility. (default "me")

inspect.description: Inspect the draft without modifying it. Returns the draft projection including subject, recipients, body summary, has_quoted_content (whether the draft contains a reply/forward quote block), attachments_summary (with part_id and cid for each attachment), and inline_summary. Run this BEFORE editing body to check has_quoted_content: if true, use set_reply_body in --patch-file to preserve the quote; if false, use set_body.

jq.description: jq expression to filter JSON output

mailbox.description: Mailbox email address that owns the draft (default: falls back to --from, then me). Takes priority over --from when both are set.

patch-file.description: Advanced edit entry point for body edits, incremental recipient changes, header edits, attachment changes, or inline-image changes. Use --body/--body-file for quick full-body replacement; use --patch-file with set_body/set_reply_body when you need typed body ops, especially set_reply_body to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block. Run --inspect first to check has_quoted_content, then --print-patch-template for the JSON structure. Relative path only.

print-patch-template.description: Print the JSON template and supported operations for the --patch-file flag. Recommended first step before generating a patch file. No draft read or write is performed.

remove-event.description: Remove the calendar event from the draft.

request-receipt.description: Request a read receipt (Message Disposition Notification, RFC 3798) addressed to the draft's sender. Recipient mail clients may prompt the user, send automatically, or silently ignore — delivery of a receipt is not guaranteed. Adds the Disposition-Notification-To header; existing value is overwritten.

set-bcc.description: Replace the entire Bcc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.

set-cc.description: Replace the entire Cc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.

set-event-summary.description: Set calendar event title. Must be used together with --set-event-start and --set-event-end.

set-priority.description: Set email priority: high, normal, low. Setting 'normal' removes any existing priority header.

set-subject.description: Replace the subject with this final value. Use this for full subject replacement, not for appending a fragment to the existing subject.

set-to.description: Replace the entire To recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.

show-lint-details.description: Include lint metadata (lint_applied[] / original_blocked[]) in the envelope. Default: no lint fields are returned to keep the envelope small.

  -q, --jq string                   jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                        shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string              Mailbox email address that owns the draft (default: falls back to --from, then me). Takes priority over --from when both are set.
      --patch-file string           Advanced edit entry point for body edits, incremental recipient changes, header edits, attachment changes, or inline-image changes. Use --body/--body-file for quick full-body replacement; use --patch-file with set_body/set_reply_body when you need typed body ops, especially set_reply_body to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block. Run --inspect first to check has_quoted_content, then --print-patch-template for the JSON structure. Relative path only.
      --print-patch-template        Print the JSON template and supported operations for the --patch-file flag. Recommended first step before generating a patch file. No draft read or write is performed.
      --remove-event                Remove the calendar event from the draft.

Recipient mail clients may prompt the user, send automatically, or silently ignore — delivery of a receipt is not guaranteed. Adds the Disposition-Notification-To header; existing value is overwritten.
      --set-bcc string              Replace the entire Bcc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-cc string               Replace the entire Cc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-event-end string        Set calendar event end time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-location string   Set calendar event location.
      --set-event-start string      Set calendar event start time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-summary string    Set calendar event title. Must be used together with --set-event-start and --set-event-end.

      --set-to string               Replace the entire To recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.

Get Mail Thread Message List

Risk: read

Full parameter schema:
  lark-cli schema mail.user_mailbox.threads.get
Parameters set via --params (no typed flag; the name is taken by another flag):
  format: --params '{"format": "full"}'
      Specifies the returned mail content format. Supported values: full, plain_text_full, and metadata. Default: full, which returns complete content such as labels, folders, subject, sender, HTML body, and plain text body
      enum: full=全文，包括标签、文件夹、主题、收发件人、纯文本、HTML等信息|plain_text_full=全文，只返回纯文本正文内容，不返回HTML|metadata=邮件元数据信息，包括标签、文件夹、主题、收发件人、摘要等信息，不返回正文内容
      do not use --format (output format: json|ndjson|table|csv)

Usage:
  lark-cli mail user_mailbox.threads get [flags]

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --thread-id string         Mail thread ID. It can be obtained through the interface return value of sending mail, replying to mail, or getting mail details interface query
      --user-mailbox-id string   User email address. When accessing as a user, you can enter "me" to represent the current calling interface user
  Optional:
      --include-spam-trash   Whether to include messages from the spam folder (SPAM) and trash folder (TRASH). true means include them. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

Raw Parameter Input:
      --params string   Raw URL/query params JSON. Supports - and @file. If both set, typed flags override matching keys in --params.

Execution:
      --as string   identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run     print request without executing

entries.help:
Add, update, or delete todo item(s) on a minute

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Write AI todos that live inside a minute — not Lark Task list items.

Avoid when:
  • Personal or shared Task lists → use the task domain (`lark-cli task`), not this shortcut

Prerequisites:
  • `minute_token` from `+search`, a minutes URL, or VC recording
  • For update/delete: `todo_id` from `+detail` with `--todo`

Tips:
  • Single todo: `--operation add --todo "..." --is-done=false`.
  • Batch: `--todos '[{"operation":"add","content":"...","is_done":false}, ...]'` or `--todos @todos.json`.
  • Batch can mix add, update, and delete in one request; array order is preserved in the API body.
  • Update: `--operation update --todo-id <id> --todo "..." --is-done`.
  • Delete: `--operation delete --todo-id <id>`.
  • `content` is plain text only; markdown formatting is not supported.
  • Use `lark-cli minutes +detail --minute-tokens <token> --todo` to read current todos before writing.

Examples:
  • Add one unfinished todo
      lark-cli minutes +todo --minute-token obcnxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx --operation add --todo "跟进预算审批" --is-done=false --as user

To write selected values into a multi-select dropdown cell, use `multiple_values:[{"value":...}]`; do not join multiple options with commas into one `value`. Run `--print-schema` for full fields (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

copy-to-range.description: Copy-to range (A1 notation): replicate what --cells wrote into --range (values/formulas/styles, per the fields actually passed) to this range; formula refs auto-shift (C2=B2 -> C3=B3). Write a one-row/one-block template then fill a whole column/area. Supports full rows '3:6', full columns 'C:E', to-col-end 'D3:D', to-row-end 'D3:3', and comma-separated multiple targets like 'C1:D2,E5:F6'.

entries.help:
Write values / formulas / styles / comments / data validation / embed-image to a cell range.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +cells-set [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-overwrite                              Allow overwriting non-empty cells (default true); set false to error if any target cell is non-empty (default true)
      --as string                                    identity type: user | bot
      --cells [[{cell},...],...]                     JSON 2D array [[{cell},...],...]; a bare `--range A1` (or `--start-cell`) is the top-left ANCHOR and this array supplies the extent; a `--range` that states a rectangle (`A1:B2`) BOUNDS the write — a smaller array narrows it, and a larger one is refused rather than written past the range. Each cell may carry `value` / `formula` / `multiple_values` / `cell_styles` / `note` / `rich_text` (incl. `type="embed-image"` in-cell image). To write selected values into a multi-select dropdown cell, use `multiple_values:[{"value":...}]`; do not join multiple options with commas into one `value`. Run `--print-schema` for full fields (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --copy-to-range string                         Copy-to range (A1 notation): replicate what --cells wrote into --range (values/formulas/styles, per the fields actually passed) to this range; formula refs auto-shift (C2=B2 -> C3=B3). Write a one-row/one-block template then fill a whole column/area. Supports full rows '3:6', full columns 'C:E', to-col-end 'D3:D', to-row-end 'D3:3', and comma-separated multiple targets like 'C1:D2,E5:F6'.
      --dry-run                                      print request without executing
      --flag-name string                             flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string                                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                                         help for +cells-set
  -q, --jq string                                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                                         shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema                                 print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --range --writes                               Write range (A1 notation). XOR with --writes (single region: --range+--cells; multiple regions: --writes)
      --sheet-id --sheet-name                        Sheet reference_id — required: pass this or --sheet-name (exactly one of the two); with `--writes` it is the default sheet for items that carry no selector of their own
      --sheet-name --sheet-id                        Sheet name — required: pass this or --sheet-id (exactly one of the two); with `--writes` it is the default sheet for items that carry no selector of their own
      --spreadsheet-token --url                      Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --url --spreadsheet-token                      Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)
      --writes {sheet_name|sheet_id, range, cells}   Multi-region write as a JSON array (up to 100 items), each {sheet_name|sheet_id, range, cells} — an item going to another sheet carries its own sheet selector (same convention as +batch-update sub-ops and +styles-put items); an item without one falls back to the top-level --sheet-name / --sheet-id. cells has the same shape as `--cells` (2D array; per-cell cell_styles/border_styles allowed). The whole array goes out as ONE batched request (fail-fast; read back to confirm what applied before resending), cross-sheet supported; typical use: fixing formulas scattered across ranges/sheets — do not assemble a +batch-update operations array for this. XOR with `--range`+`--cells`; range-level uniform styling stays with +styles-put afterwards (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Example: lark-cli sheets +cells-set --url <URL> --sheet-name Sheet1 --range A1:B1 --cells '[[{"value":"名称"},{"formula":"=SUM(B2:B9)"}]]'
    • --cells is always a 2D array (rows × cells), even for one cell: [[{"value":…}]].
    • Scattered regions (e.g. fixing formulas across ranges/sheets): --writes '[{"sheet_name":…,"range":…,"cells":[[…]]}, …]' — one batch request (fail-fast, no rollback), sheet selector inside each item.

entries.description: Create a basic chart from a chart type and data range; the server builds and validates the full snapshot.

aggregate-categories.description: Whether to aggregate duplicate categories; use --aggregate-categories=false for sparse markers or row-level data points, and omit it to use the chart default

anchor-cell.description: Optional chart anchor cell such as F2; defaults to the right of the data range

color-palette.description: Preset chart-level color palette; mutually exclusive with --colors (brandColorSeries@v2|rainbowColorSeries@v2|complementaryColorSeries@v2|converseColorSeries@v2|primaryColorSeries@v2|singleColorSeries-B-@v2|singleColorSeries-W-@v2|singleColorSeries-G-@v2|singleColorSeries-Y-@v2|singleColorSeries-O-@v2|singleColorSeries-R-@v2|singleColorSeries-D-@v2)

colors.description: Custom chart-level series colors as a comma-separated list of at least two hex colors; mutually exclusive with --color-palette

data-direction.description: Data series direction; column uses the first column as categories, row uses the first row (column|row) (default "column")

data-label-position.description: For an ordinary non-stacked column chart with labels, generally pass outside; in other cases, pass only when the user explicitly requests a position; this only repositions existing labels and does not enable them (auto|top|bottom|left|right|center|inside|outside)

data-labels.description: Data label content; pass value by default for a basic chart and do not omit it solely because there are many data points or series; pass none only when the user explicitly requests hiding all labels; combine value, category, and percentage in value_category_percentage order for any non-empty combination; series shows series names (none|value|category|percentage|value_category|value_percentage|category_percentage|value_category_percentage|series)

data-range.description: (required) Data range; include headers unless --header-range is set, in which case pass data only; accepts comma-separated ranges across one or more sheets

dim1-index.description: 1-based index of the single supported category/X-axis dimension within the data range; defaults to 1; multiple fields cannot form a multi-level X-axis

dim2-indexes.description: Comma-separated 1-based value/Y-axis dimension indexes; must exclude dim1, at most 50. Legacy bubble calls accept 2–4 indexes in x,y[,group][,size] order; new calls should use role-specific indexes. Pie and pareto charts accept exactly one

format.description: output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")

group-index.description: Bubble only: optional 1-based group dimension index

header-range.description: Optional detached header range; use one row for column direction or one column for row direction, with one header per data dimension

height.description: Optional chart height; must be paired with --width

jq.description: jq expression to filter JSON output

key-index.description: Bubble only: 1-based key/name dimension index; mutually exclusive with dim1/dim2 indexes; defaults to 1

legend-position.description: Legend position; use bottom by default for pie charts; hidden removes the legend (top|bottom|left|right|hidden)

series-types.description: Combo charts only; comma-separated series types aligned with --dim2-indexes; use column, line, area, or scatter and provide one value per selected series

series-y-axes.description: Combo charts only; compare series units and magnitudes first and place a series that would be flattened on the right axis; pass left or right aligned with --dim2-indexes, one value per selected series

sheet-id.description: Sheet reference_id (XOR with --sheet-name)

sheet-name.description: Sheet name (XOR with --sheet-id)

size-index.description: Bubble only: optional 1-based bubble-size dimension index

smooth.description: Use smooth curves; pass --smooth=false to disable explicitly

width.description: Optional chart width; must be paired with --height; widen pie charts and charts with long category labels to avoid truncation

entries.help:
Create a basic chart from a chart type and data range; the server builds and validates the full snapshot.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +chart-create-basic [flags]

Flags:
      --aggregate-categories              Whether to aggregate duplicate categories; use --aggregate-categories=false for sparse markers or row-level data points, and omit it to use the chart default
      --anchor-cell string                Optional chart anchor cell such as F2; defaults to the right of the data range
      --as string                         identity type: user | bot
      --chart-type string                 (required) Chart type (column|bar|line|area|pie|scatter|combo|radar|bubble|waterfall|pareto)
      --color-palette string              Preset chart-level color palette; mutually exclusive with --colors (brandColorSeries@v2|rainbowColorSeries@v2|complementaryColorSeries@v2|converseColorSeries@v2|primaryColorSeries@v2|singleColorSeries-B-@v2|singleColorSeries-W-@v2|singleColorSeries-G-@v2|singleColorSeries-Y-@v2|singleColorSeries-O-@v2|singleColorSeries-R-@v2|singleColorSeries-D-@v2)
      --colors strings                    Custom chart-level series colors as a comma-separated list of at least two hex colors; mutually exclusive with --color-palette
      --data-direction string             Data series direction; column uses the first column as categories, row uses the first row (column|row) (default "column")
      --data-label-position string        For an ordinary non-stacked column chart with labels, generally pass outside; in other cases, pass only when the user explicitly requests a position; this only repositions existing labels and does not enable them (auto|top|bottom|left|right|center|inside|outside)
      --data-labels string                Data label content; pass value by default for a basic chart and do not omit it solely because there are many data points or series; pass none only when the user explicitly requests hiding all labels; combine value, category, and percentage in value_category_percentage order for any non-empty combination; series shows series names (none|value|category|percentage|value_category|value_percentage|category_percentage|value_category_percentage|series)
      --data-range string                 (required) Data range; include headers unless --header-range is set, in which case pass data only; accepts comma-separated ranges across one or more sheets
      --dim1-index int                    1-based index of the single supported category/X-axis dimension within the data range; defaults to 1; multiple fields cannot form a multi-level X-axis
      --dim2-indexes x,y[,group][,size]   Comma-separated 1-based value/Y-axis dimension indexes; must exclude dim1, at most 50. Legacy bubble calls accept 2–4 indexes in x,y[,group][,size] order; new calls should use role-specific indexes. Pie and pareto charts accept exactly one
      --dry-run                           print request without executing
      --format string                     output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
      --group-index int                   Bubble only: optional 1-based group dimension index
      --header-range string               Optional detached header range; use one row for column direction or one column for row direction, with one header per data dimension
      --height int                        Optional chart height; must be paired with --width
  -h, --help                              help for +chart-create-basic
  -q, --jq string                         jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                              shorthand for --format json
      --key-index int                     Bubble only: 1-based key/name dimension index; mutually exclusive with dim1/dim2 indexes; defaults to 1
      --legend-position string            Legend position; use bottom by default for pie charts; hidden removes the legend (top|bottom|left|right|hidden)
      --secondary-y-axis-title string     Right Y-axis title
      --series-types string               Combo charts only; comma-separated series types aligned with --dim2-indexes; use column, line, area, or scatter and provide one value per selected series
      --series-y-axes string              Combo charts only; compare series units and magnitudes first and place a series that would be flattened on the right axis; pass left or right aligned with --dim2-indexes, one value per selected series
      --sheet-id --sheet-name             Sheet reference_id (XOR with --sheet-name)
      --sheet-name --sheet-id             Sheet name (XOR with --sheet-id)
      --size-index int                    Bubble only: optional 1-based bubble-size dimension index
      --smooth                            Use smooth curves; pass --smooth=false to disable explicitly
      --spreadsheet-token --url           Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --stack string                      Stacking mode (none|normal|percent)
      --subtitle string                   Chart subtitle
      --title string                      Chart title
      --url --spreadsheet-token           Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)
      --width int                         Optional chart width; must be paired with --height; widen pie charts and charts with long category labels to avoid truncation
      --x-axis-label-angle int            X-axis label angle (-90|-45|0|45|90)
      --x-axis-max float                  Upper display bound for a continuous numeric X-axis; requires --x-axis-numbers-as values
      --x-axis-min float                  Lower display bound for a continuous numeric X-axis; requires --x-axis-numbers-as values
      --x-axis-numbers-as string          How to interpret numeric X-axis values; text treats numbers as evenly spaced text categories, while values uses a continuous numeric scale and preserves true spacing (text|values) (default "text")
      --x-axis-title string               X-axis title
      --x-index int                       Bubble only: 1-based X-value dimension index; must be provided with --y-index
      --y-axis-label-angle int            Left Y-axis label angle (-90|-45|0|45|90)
      --y-axis-max float                  Upper display bound for the left Y-axis; omit by default and pass together with --y-axis-min only when the user explicitly requests fixed bounds; calculate it from rendered chart semantics, and keep it above the lower bound
      --y-axis-min float                  Lower display bound for the left Y-axis; omit by default and pass together with --y-axis-max only when the user explicitly requests fixed bounds; do not copy a raw source-column minimum, and keep it below the upper bound
      --y-axis-title string               Left Y-axis title
      --y-index int                       Bubble only: 1-based Y-value dimension index; must be provided with --x-index

Risk: write

print-schema.description: print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing

range.description: Column closed range to resize; column letters like A:E or `C` (single column). Required for the uniform form (with `--width` or `--type`); omit with the map form (`--widths`)

type.description: Sizing mode: pixel (requires `--width`) / `standard` (reset to default column width). Passing --width alone is the common form; `--type standard` cannot be combined with `--width` (pixel|standard)

width.description: Uniform column width in pixels (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200; NOT Excel character units), used with --range. Passing --width implies pixel mode; --type may be omitted (or set to `pixel` — equivalent). For per-column widths use `--widths`

widths.description: Per-column width map — set different widths for many columns in one batched call (fail-fast; read back before resending). Keys: single column ("A") or closed range (`"C:E"`); values: pixel width (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200) or `"standard"` (reset to default). Units are pixels, NOT Excel character units (px ≈ chars × 8 + 16). Mutually exclusive with `--range` / `--width` / `--type` (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

max-chars.description: Max output chars per call; default 500000 (safety cap). For a full untruncated read, use --output-path to dump to a file (the cap auto-raises to a bounded 20M chars — the read path is not streaming, this cap is the memory guard; pass an explicit --max-chars for more); only lower it (e.g. 25000) when you want results inline without a file, paging via has_more. Passing 0 means "no cap of my own" and resolves to the same ceiling as leaving the flag alone (500000, or the offload limit with --output-path) — never down to the tool's smaller omitted-value fallback. (default 500000)

output-path.description: Write the full read result to a local path (e.g. ./out.json); the file holds the data payload as JSON while stdout returns only a small confirmation (output_path, byte count). **When set, the char cap auto-raises to a bounded offload default (20M chars)** rather than unlimited — the read path is not streaming, so this cap is the memory guard; an explicit --max-chars overrides it. The stdout receipt reports `complete` (and `truncated` plus a warning when the cap was hit), so check it instead of assuming the file holds the whole sheet. Note the file is the data payload as JSON — on +csv-get too, where the CSV text sits in a field inside it — not a ready-to-use .csv; redirect stdout instead if you want a bare CSV file. Omit it to print to stdout as usual.

range.description: A1 range, e.g. A1:F30 (no sheet prefix — use `--sheet-id` / `--sheet-name` to select the sheet).       --range F1                               Pivot table top-left placement (single A1 value, e.g. F1; create only), maps to `properties.range`; placed at the top-left of the target sub-sheet (a newly created one by default) when omitted. It lands on the same wire field as `--target-position`; passing a non-default value for both is rejected — pass only one.
      --source 'SheetName'!StartCell:EndCell   (required) Pivot table source range (A1 notation; format 'SheetName'!StartCell:EndCell, e.g. `'Sheet1'!A1:D100`)
      --spreadsheet-token --url                Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --target-position A1                     Top-left cell within the target sub-sheet (A1 notation, e.g. A1), default `A1` (not sent when the value is A1). It lands on the same wire field as `--range` (`properties.range`) and takes precedence when non-default; passing a non-default value for both is rejected — pass only one. (default "A1")
      --target-sheet-id --target-sheet-name    Reference_id of the target sub-sheet where the pivot table will be placed (mutually exclusive with --target-sheet-name; takes priority when both given; when both omitted, a new sub-sheet is auto-created to host the pivot — recommended). Distinct from the data-source sheet, which lives inside --source as a 'Sheet'-prefixed A1 reference like 'Sheet1'!A1:D100.
      --target-sheet-name --target-sheet-id    Name of the target sub-sheet where the pivot table will be placed (mutually exclusive with --target-sheet-id; when both omitted, a new sub-sheet is auto-created to host the pivot — recommended). Distinct from the data-source sheet, which lives inside --source as a 'Sheet'-prefixed A1 reference like 'Sheet1'!A1:D100.
      --url --spreadsheet-token                Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Placement: omit --target-sheet-id / --target-sheet-name and the backend auto-creates a fresh sub-sheet for the pivot — zero overwrite risk. This is the default and the recommended path.
    • Only pass --target-sheet-id/-name to land in an existing sheet; if that sheet holds the source data you MUST set --target-position (or --range) outside the data, else the pivot overwrites it and the anchor shows #REF!.
    • Removing a stray pivot is +pivot-delete (get its id from +pivot-list); +cells-clear / +cells-batch-clear only clear cell values/formats and cannot delete the pivot object.

height.description: Uniform row height in pixels (e.g. 30 / 40 / 60; NOT points), used with --range. Passing --height implies pixel mode; --type may be omitted (or set to `pixel` — equivalent). For per-row heights use `--heights`

heights.description: Per-row height map — set different heights for many rows in one batched call (fail-fast; read back before resending). Keys: single row ("1") or closed range (`"2:20"`); values: pixel height (e.g. 30 / 50), `"auto"` (fit content) or `"standard"` (reset to default). Units are pixels, NOT points. max-chars.description: Max output chars per call; default 500000 (safety cap). The underlying tool truncates at ~50000 even when unset, so this is sent explicitly to raise it; for a full untruncated read use --output-path (cap auto-raises to a bounded 20M chars; explicit --max-chars overrides). Passing 0 means "no cap of my own" and resolves to the same ceiling as leaving the flag alone (500000, or the offload limit with --output-path) — never down to the tool's smaller omitted-value fallback. (default 500000)

no-header.description: Treat the first row as data instead of a header (columns get positional names col1, col2, ...)

output-path.description: Write the full read result to a local path (e.g. ./out.json); the file holds the data payload as JSON while stdout returns only a small confirmation (output_path, byte count). **When set, the char cap auto-raises to a bounded offload default (20M chars)** rather than unlimited — the read path is not streaming, so this cap is the memory guard; an explicit --max-chars overrides it. The stdout receipt reports `complete` (and `truncated` plus a warning when the cap was hit), so check it instead of assuming the file holds the whole sheet. Omit it to print to stdout as usual.

range.description: A1 range to read; omit to read each sheet's full used range (spans internal blank rows/columns, not just the A1 current region)

sheet-id.description: Read only this sheet (by id); omit to read all sheets

sheets.description: (required) Typed table payload (pandas-DataFrame-shaped) as JSON: top-level {"sheets":[...]}, with each array item a sub-sheet `{name, start_cell?, mode?, header?, allow_overwrite?, columns:["colA","colB",...], data:[[...]], dtypes?:{colA:pandasDtype, ...}, formats?:{colA:numberFormat, ...}}` — `name` and the outer `sheets` envelope are both required. Agents typically use `df_to_sheet(df, name)` from `scripts/lark_sheets_df.py` to pack each DataFrame into one item, then wrap the list in `{"sheets":[...]}`. `dtypes` values are pandas dtype strings (`int64`, `float64`, `Int64`, `bool`, `boolean`, `datetime64[ns]`, `object`, ...); the writer maps them to internal string/number/date/bool — omit `dtypes` and a column writes as text (good for raw CSV-shaped data). `formats[col]` is an Excel number_format string (e.g. `#,##0.00`, `0.0%`, `yyyy-mm`); when absent, date columns default to `yyyy-mm-dd` and string columns to text format (`@`). ios.description: custom completion configuration of pc(include mac and windows)

custom_fields.description: Custom field values. If updted, the values needs to be set to the corresponding field according to the field type.;* When `type` is "number", the `number_value` field should be used to represent the value of number custom fields; * When "type" is "member", the `member_value` field should be used to represent the value of member custom field; * When `type` is "datetime", `datetime_value` field should be used to represent the value of the datetime custom field.;* When `type` is "single_select", the `single_select_value` field should be used to represent the value of single_select custom field.;* When `type` is "multi_select", the `multi_select_value` field should be used to represent the value of multi_select custom field.;* When `type` is "text", the `text_value` field should be used to represent the value of text custom field

multi_select_value.description: 多选类型字段值，可以填写一个或多个本字段的option_guid。设为空数组表示设为空

number_value.description: 数字类型的自定义字段值，填写一个合法数字的字符串表示，空字符串表示设为空

single_select_value.description: 单选类型字段值，填写一个字段选项的option_guid。设置为空字符串表示设为空

text_value.description: 文本类型字段值。可以填写最多3000字符。使用空字符串表示设为空
text_value.example: 文本类型字段值。可以输入一段文本。空字符串表示清空。

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the due time/date in milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. If the due time is a date, convert the date to a timestamp and set is_all_day = true

extra.description: 调用者可以传入的任意附带到任务上的数据。在获取任务详情时会原样返回

mode.description: 任务的完成模式。1 - 会签任务；2 - 或签任务

repeat_rule.description: 如果设置，则该任务为“重复任务”。该字段表示了重复任务的重复规则

is_all_day.description: Whether to start on a date. If set to true, only the date part of the timestamp will be parsed and stored

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the start time/date in milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00. If the start time is a date, convert the date to a timestamp and set is_all_day = true.; If both the start time and the due time are set, the start time must be <= the due time, and the is_all_day settings of the start and due times must be the same

update_fields.description: Fields to modify; supported values:;- summary: task title;- description: task description;- start: task start time;- due: task due time;- completed_at: task completion time;- extra: task attached custom data;- custom_complete: task custom completion rule;- repeat_rule: task repeat rule;- mode: task completion mode;- is_milestone: whether the task is a milestone;- custom_fields: custom field values
